title: STAAR Science Task Cards
subject: science
description: 32 TEKS-Aligned STAAR Science Task Cards for 8th Grade

questions.question: An element has an atomic number of 12 and a mass number of 24. How many protons, neutrons, and electrons does a neutral atom of this element have?
Use the portion of the periodic table shown. Which two elements would have the MOST similar chemical properties?
In the chemical equation 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, what do the coefficients represent?
choices: A) The number of atoms in each molecule
B) The number of molecules involved in the reaction
C) The atomic mass of each element
D) The speed of the reaction

questions.question: A student performs four different tests in the lab. Which observation provides evidence that a chemical change has occurred?
choices: C) A nail rusting when left outside
D) Cutting a piece of paper in half

questions.question: Students tested four substances and recorded their observations. Which substance MOST LIKELY underwent a chemical change?

rows: No color change, no gas produced

questions.question: A 2 kg ball is kicked with a force of 10 N. What is the acceleration of the ball? (Use F = ma)
A box is being pushed to the right with a force of 50 N. Friction pushes back with a force of 30 N. What is the net force and direction of the box's acceleration?
According to Newton's Third Law, when a swimmer pushes water backward with her hands, what happens?
choices: A) The water pushes the swimmer backward
B) Nothing happens to the swimmer
C) The water pushes the swimmer forward with an equal force

questions.question: A student records the position of a toy car every 2 seconds. Based on the graph, during which time interval was the car moving the fastest?
A car travels 150 kilometers in 3 hours. What is the average speed of the car?
The graph shows the motion of two runners during a race. Which statement is BEST supported by the data?
choices: A) Runner A had a constant speed the entire race
B) Runner A accelerated during the race while Runner B had constant speed
C) Runner B was faster than Runner A at all times
D) Both runners had the same average speed

questions.question: A wave has a frequency of 5 Hz and a wavelength of 3 meters. What is the speed of the wave? (Use v = f x wavelength)
Students measured the wavelength and frequency of four different waves. Which wave has the GREATEST speed?
Which layer of Earth is responsible for the movement of tectonic plates?
The data table shows observations from a plate boundary. What type of plate boundary is MOST LIKELY described?
choices: D) No plate boundary exists here

rows: Chain of volcanic mountains parallel to coast
Older rocks on land, younger near trench

questions.question: Which event would MOST LIKELY occur at a divergent plate boundary?
choices: A) A deep ocean trench forms
C) One plate slides under another
D) New ocean floor is created at a mid-ocean ridge

questions.question: Which of the following correctly lists objects in our universe from SMALLEST to LARGEST?
choices: A) Galaxy, Solar System, Star, Planet
B) Star, Planet, Galaxy, Solar System
C) Planet, Star, Solar System, Galaxy
D) Solar System, Planet, Star, Galaxy

questions.question: A student collects data on the planets in our solar system. Based on the data, which planet would have the STRONGEST gravitational pull on an object on its surface?
Which cell structure is found in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
A student observes cells under a microscope and records the following data. Which sample is MOST LIKELY from a plant?
In humans, brown eye color (B) is dominant over blue eye color (b). A father with genotype Bb and a mother with genotype Bb have a child. What is the probability that the child will have blue eyes?

A Punnett square is used to predict offspring traits. Two parents who are both heterozygous (Rr) for round seed shape are crossed. The data table shows the expected results. What percentage of offspring are expected to have round seeds?

In an ecosystem, grass captures energy from the sun. Grasshoppers eat the grass. Frogs eat the grasshoppers. Snakes eat the frogs. Which organism in this food chain has the LEAST amount of available energy?
The bar graph shows the amount of energy available at each trophic level in an ecosystem. Approximately what percentage of energy is transferred from producers to primary consumers?

A population of beetles lives on a dark forest floor. Some beetles are dark-colored and some are light-colored. Birds eat the beetles they can see. Over many generations, what will MOST LIKELY happen?
choices: A) All beetles will become light-colored
B) The population will have more dark-colored beetles
C) The birds will stop eating beetles
D) The beetles will grow larger to avoid predators

questions.question: Scientists tracked a beetle population over 50 years. The data shows the percentage of dark-colored beetles over time. Which concept BEST explains the trend shown?
Which factor is MOST responsible for the differences in climate between a city near the equator and a city near the North Pole?
Students collected average temperature and precipitation data for four cities. Which city MOST LIKELY has a desert climate?
A student tracks the movement of a cold front on a weather map. Which weather conditions would the student MOST LIKELY observe as the cold front passes through their area?
choices: A) Clear skies and rising temperatures
B) Heavy rain, thunderstorms, then cooler temperatures
C) Fog and steady drizzle for several days
D) No change in weather conditions

questions.question: A factory releases large amounts of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. Which long-term effect is this MOST LIKELY to contribute to?
choices: A) Increase in average global temperatures

questions.question: The graph shows carbon dioxide levels and average global temperature over 60 years. What relationship is BEST supported by the data?
choices: A) As CO₂ increases, average global temperature also increases
B) CO₂ levels and temperature are not related
C) As CO₂ increases, temperature decreases
